title: "Student Alcohol Consumption - Solutions"
output: html_document

### Introduction:

This time you will download a dataset from the UCI.

In pandas this exercise uses `apply()`; in R the same idea is covered by
vectorised functions inside `mutate()`, `across()` and the `purrr::map()` family.

### Step 1. Import the necessary libraries

```{r step1, message=FALSE}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
```

### Step 2. Import the dataset from this [address](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guipsamora/pandas_exercises/master/04_Apply/Students_Alcohol_Consumption/student-mat.csv).

### Step 3. Assign it to a variable called df.

```{r}
# the same file is also included in this folder: read_csv("student-mat.csv")
csv_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guipsamora/pandas_exercises/master/04_Apply/Students_Alcohol_Consumption/student-mat.csv"
df <- read_csv(csv_url)
head(df)
```

### Step 4. For the purpose of this exercise slice the dataframe from 'school' until the 'guardian' column

```{r}
stud_alcoh <- df |> select(school:guardian)
head(stud_alcoh)
```

### Step 5. Create a lambda function that will capitalize strings.

```{r}
# str_to_sentence() puts the first letter in upper case and the rest in lower case
capitalizer <- \(x) str_to_sentence(x)
```

### Step 6. Capitalize both Mjob and Fjob

```{r}
capitalizer(stud_alcoh$Mjob) |> head()
capitalizer(stud_alcoh$Fjob) |> head()
```

### Step 7. Print the last elements of the data set.

```{r}
tail(stud_alcoh)
```

### Step 8. Did you notice the original dataframe is still lowercase? Why is that? Fix it and capitalize Mjob and Fjob.

```{r}
# R never modifies an object "in place": the result has to be assigned back
stud_alcoh <- stud_alcoh |> mutate(across(c(Mjob, Fjob), capitalizer))
tail(stud_alcoh)
```

### Step 9. Create a function called majority that returns a boolean value to a new column called legal_drinker (Consider majority as older than 17 years old)

```{r}
majority <- function(x) {
  x > 17
}
```

```{r}
stud_alcoh <- stud_alcoh |> mutate(legal_drinker = majority(age))
head(stud_alcoh)
```

### Step 10. Multiply every number of the dataset by 10.

##### I know this makes no sense, don't forget it is just an exercise

```{r}
times10 <- function(x) {
  10 * x
}
```

```{r}
stud_alcoh |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), times10)) |>
  head(10)
```
